is-this-page-for-you.h2: Are you the worker or the employer?

blocks.x: Most sponsorship cases involve both. The employer sponsors and nominates. The worker applies for the visa. Each visa page below shows what applies to each side.
**Workers and graduates.** You have a job offer and want to know which visa applies, or you hold a 482 and want to reach permanent residence.

**Employers.** You cannot fill a role locally, you have never sponsored before, or you sponsor already and need help with nominations, renewals or compliance. Start with the [Application Process Guide](/employer-sponsored/application-process-guide).
Most employer sponsored visas follow the same three stages. Each stage has its own forms, charges and processing time.

head: Stage
Who does it
What it means
rows: The business applies to become an approved sponsor. The Department checks that it is genuine and lawful.
The business nominates a specific position, usually with a named worker, and shows the job is genuine and pays enough.
The worker applies once the nomination is lodged or approved. Health, character, skills and English are checked.

blocks.label: Note
blocks.x: The order of nomination and visa lodgement varies by visa. A few visas, such as the Short Stay Specialist 400, need no sponsorship. Read the [Application Process Guide](/employer-sponsored/application-process-guide) for the full sequence.

Processing has three parts: the sponsor application, the nomination and the visa application. Check the Department of Home Affairs website for current processing times, which change often. Some streams and occupations get priority.
**Employers:** allow several months from the day you decide to sponsor to the day the worker can start. Do not set a start date you cannot move.

The most common route is the [ENS 186 Temporary Residence Transition stream](/employer-sponsored/ens-186-trt). In general you need two years of full-time work for your sponsor on a 482, and your employer must nominate you again for a permanent role.

Other routes include the [Direct Entry stream](/employer-sponsored/ens-186-direct), state nominated visas through our [skilled migration pages](/migrate-to-australia) and the [regional 191](/migrate-to-australia/permanent-residence-skilled-regional-visa-subclass-191). The best route depends on your occupation, age and points. Use the [PR Points Calculator](/migrate-to-australia/pr-point-calculator).
**Changing employers.** You can usually move to a new sponsor if the new employer nominates you within the time allowed.

the-honest-path-course-visa-work-graduat.h2: The path: course, visa, then PR only if you qualify

blocks.x: Study can be part of a pathway to permanent residence, but it is never automatic.

items.x: **Choose a course.** Pick a CRICOS-registered course that fits your past study, work and future plans. See [Admission in Australia](/study-australia/admission-in-australia).
**Get your Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE).** Your provider issues it after you accept your offer. See [New CoE](/study-australia/new-coe).

**Apply for the Subclass 500 student visa.** You need your CoE, health cover, English, funds and a clear Genuine Student statement. See [Student visa information](/study-australia/student-visa-information).
**Study within your visa conditions.** Student visas have work limits during study periods.

**Graduate and look at your next visa.** Some graduates may qualify for the [Temporary Graduate visa 485](/migrate-to-australia/temporary-graduate-visa-subclass-485). The rules and age limits have changed recently.

**Consider skilled migration.** If your occupation, skills assessment and points are right, you may be able to apply for a skilled visa. Use the [PR Points Calculator](/migrate-to-australia/pr-point-calculator). A Professional Year can add points for some graduates.

blocks.label: Note
blocks.x: Choosing a course only to reach PR is a risk. The Department looks at whether your study makes sense for you.
